source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

rural.evidence: Royal Enfield retail footprint expanded from 1,521 stores/1,200 cities to 2,056 stores/1,750 cities, with network growth described across 'urban as well as rural markets'; no revenue percentage split disclosed in sources reviewed.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY2025: domestic sales 902,757 units (+8.1% YoY) vs exports 100,136 units (+29.7% YoY) out of total 1,002,893 Royal Enfield units sold, implying ~10% export/USD-linked volume mix. No explicit hedging policy disclosure located.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company described as leading India's push for rare-earth/magnet supply independence as China tightens export controls (relevant to EV motor inputs); recent acquisitions described as expected to 'shift the majority of revenues to India, helping insulate the company from regional supply chain disruptions.' Note: Sona also signed a JV term sheet with a Chinese firm (Jinnaite Machinery) to manufacture driveline systems in China -- an expansion INTO China rather than a pure derisking-from-China narrative, so not scored 'strong'.

crude_exposure.evidence: Forged/machined steel driveline and motor components; no explicit crude-linked raw material percentage disclosed in sources reviewed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Geographic revenue mix (most recent disclosed, Q2 FY26 investor deck, used as proxy for FY25 given no separate FY25-only breakdown found): India 41%, North America 30%, Europe 24%, other ~5%.

pli_scheme.evidence: Sona Comstar became the first automotive component manufacturer to receive certification under the Auto PLI scheme, having filed seven applications and received certification for a hub wheel drive motor for electric two-wheelers.

china_plus_one.evidence: 'Divi's plays in well as a China+1 strategy for major pharma companies as they look to de-leverage from dependence on Chinese API manufacturers... Divi's should continue benefiting from custom-synthesis order-book conversion and the structural China+1/BIOSECURE-linked tailwind.' Management guided double-digit FY26 growth citing 'stronger momentum from China+1' alongside GLP-1 commercialisation as key triggers. Separately, a 2020 Business Standard piece noted 'choke in API supplies from China creates huge opportunity for Divi's Labs.'

crude_exposure.evidence: Petrochemical/solvent-based raw materials used in API synthesis; company has emphasized backward integration into Key Starting Materials (KSMs, e.g. for Gabapentin, Naproxen, Valsartan, Levetiracetam) partly to reduce China-sourced input dependence, but no crude-linked raw material percentage disclosed in sources reviewed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports comprised ~88-90% of sales; Europe and US together account for roughly 72-74% of revenue (Europe ~58%, US ~14% per one breakdown cited in market commentary). Generic APIs ~47% of sales, custom synthesis (CDMO/contract manufacturing for global innovators) ~45% of sales.

pli_scheme.evidence: Divi's has announced PLI-supported capacity expansions in API segments (fermentation-based APIs and complex synthesis, backward integration into KSMs/bulk drugs) where Chinese pricing had previously made domestic investment unviable; no specific revenue percentage attributed to PLI disclosed in sources reviewed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Exports described as 'only 10% of the business mix,' with commentary noting operations are 'world-class, offering productivity and labor arbitrage advantages' and the company being 'export-ready,' but no explicit China+1/supply-chain-diversification framing tied to revenue growth was found.

govt_capex.evidence: Company commentary describes it as 'a beneficiary of government capex investments in mega infrastructure and renewable projects,' with record order backlog (~INR 11,094 crore per one disclosure) driven by large system/service orders from transportation, metals, energy and data-center segments; 'policy-driven public sector capex with incentivizing local production (PLI) in areas like specialty steel and battery manufacturing augmented the opportunity landscape' for ABB India's addressable market. No exact revenue percentage from government-linked capex disclosed in sources reviewed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Capital goods manufacturer (electrification/automation equipment); primary raw materials are copper, steel and electronic components rather than crude-linked inputs. No percentage disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports (foreign-currency-linked revenue) estimated at ~10% of business mix; predominantly domestic INR-denominated revenue from local capex/order execution.

pli_scheme.evidence: ABB India is characterized as benefiting indirectly from PLI-driven customer capex (e.g., specialty steel, battery manufacturing sectors investing under PLI, creating demand for ABB's electrification/automation equipment) rather than being a direct PLI scheme incentive recipient itself.

rural.evidence: MD&A/analyst commentary: 'The pace of growth of consumption in Tier-2/3/4 cities as well as rural areas could outpace that of urban cities. This would be beneficial for USL, considering its well-entrenched manufacturing and distribution footprint across India.' Growth drivers cited: low per-capita consumption, favourable demographics, up-trading from country liquor to IMFL, benefiting semi-urban/rural expansion.

crude_exposure.evidence: Company commentary on cost inflation (not crude oil directly but petrochemical-linked packaging): glass bottle costs up 11-17%, paper cartons up ~100%, PET resin (plastic) up 30-50%, plastic caps up 15-20%. ENA (extra neutral alcohol) up ~11% YoY in a recent quarter. CFO noted packaging inflation alone could cut gross margins by 1.25-1.5pp in a quarter (~INR40 crore impact); a Middle East/West Asia crisis-related cost shock of ~INR30 crore was also cited across glass, energy, packaging and logistics.

pli_scheme.evidence: Alcoholic beverages (IMFL/Scotch) are not a category covered by any Indian PLI scheme; no PLI participation found or expected.

rural.evidence: 'Rural India remains one of the company's most significant growth opportunities, given both the pace of demand expansion and the headroom to deepen presence.' Nestle India runs a 'RUrban' (rural+urban) distribution push since 2019, deepening presence in smaller towns and further penetrating rural markets from 2025. Double-digit volume growth for Maggi noodles was 'led by market share gains in rural areas'; KitKat confectionery growth also linked to distribution expansion in rural areas. Separately, management (CMD) has flagged urban demand as resilient while rural recovery depends on monsoon outcomes, farm income and government support.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 export revenue was reported at ~₹210 crore, down 9% YoY (coffee exports declined), against total FY25 net sales of ~₹19,089 crore (~1.1% of sales) - implying minimal direct USD/export revenue exposure; Nestle India does import some raw materials (e.g., green coffee) creating indirect FX cost exposure, but no explicit hedging policy percentage was found in accessible sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: Nestlé India received Government of India approval (announced ~Dec 2021) under the Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Food Processing Industry (PLISFPI) for the 'processed fruits & vegetables' category. No specific revenue or incentive percentage disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: No explicit company-sourced 'China+1' quote could be verified (direct AR PDF fetch was blocked in this environment). Industry/analyst context: India's PLI scheme for APIs/KSMs/Drug Intermediates is explicitly aimed at 'reducing dependence on countries such as China,' and Sun Pharma is commonly cited among PLI-beneficiary companies expanding API capacity. Sun Pharma's own messaging emphasizes a 'more balanced business with less dependence on any single geography' via growth in Branded Generics, Innovative Medicines, Generics and APIs - a general diversification narrative, but without explicit China+1 revenue attribution.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 revenue mix: India Formulations 33% (~Rs 169 bn), US 31% (Rs 16,240.3 crore, +5.8% YoY), Emerging Markets 18% (Rs 94,160 mn, +9.2% YoY), Rest of World Formulations 14% (Rs 71,626 mn), API & Others 4%, on total consolidated revenue of ~Rs 54,543 crore. This implies ~67% of revenue is international/export, predominantly USD or other foreign-currency denominated, but no specific hedging-policy text was located.

pli_scheme.evidence: Sun Pharma is widely cited among beneficiary companies under India's PLI Scheme for domestic manufacturing of critical KSMs/Drug Intermediates/APIs (48 projects approved nationally, ~Rs 45,158 crore scheme investment), expanding API capacity for domestic and export demand. No Sun Pharma-specific PLI revenue figure disclosed in accessible sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: Industry/analyst commentary (not a direct AR quote, direct PDF fetch was blocked): 'India's pharmaceutical industry is currently benefiting from the China+1 strategy, where global buyers are diversifying supply chains, providing a favorable effect on Emcure's export business... Emcure manufactures APIs for its own use and external sales, ensuring backward integration and supply chain stability.' Emcure is a vertically integrated manufacturer with an in-house API vertical supporting its formulations export business, but no company-sourced quote explicitly attributes specific revenue/order growth to China+1 diversification.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Emcure raised ~INR 800 crore in its July 2024 IPO, of which ~INR 600 crore was used for debt reduction. Remaining long-term debt repayment obligations of ~INR 100-180 crore are expected in FY26/FY27, to be funded via internal cash accruals. No floating-vs-fixed rate breakdown of residual debt was found.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Emcure offsets foreign currency payables (trade obligations, loans) against foreign currency receivables, creating a natural hedge across its multi-currency export book (EUR/CAD/USD and emerging-market currencies); it also monitors currency positions and may use financial instruments or operational adjustments for residual risk.
inr_exposure.evidence: 'Emcure offsets foreign currency payables—such as trade obligations and loans—against foreign currency receivables, creating a natural hedge. The company also monitors its currency positions and may use financial instruments or operational adjustments to manage residual risk.'

pli_scheme.evidence: Emcure Pharmaceuticals is cited as one of 9 domestic pharmaceutical companies approved in Group B under India's PLI Scheme for Pharmaceuticals/bulk drugs (incentive rates: 20% for fermentation-based products, 10% for chemical-based products in initial years, tapering thereafter). No Emcure-specific PLI revenue percentage disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Business Responsibility & Sustainability Report (BRSR) FY2024-25 filing: deemed export of services contributed 5.19% of total turnover in FY2024-25, compared to 4.94% in the prior year, reflecting international/foreign patient revenue at Medanta hospitals.

rural.evidence: Retail chain of 3,312 stores across 435 towns with 4.70 million sq. ft. retail area; company is focusing on expanding in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities, where it is well-positioned to capitalise on the potential slowdown of regional/unorganised players and gain market share. Jewellery demand anticipated to see an uptick given wedding season activity, with total weddings expected to cross 4.5 million in H2 vs 4.2 million in H1FY25. Domestic India jewellery business grew 23%, driven by 30% growth in gold jewellery/coins and 12% growth in studded jewellery.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Titan follows a near-100% gold hedging strategy, described as among the highest in the industry, protecting it from gold price volatility (vs. ~60% of the unorganised market that does not hedge or only partially hedges). RBI has permitted Titan to hedge its gold inventory and currency futures on international exchanges to manage currency/forex exposure arising from gold imports.
inr_exposure.evidence: Government of India raised customs duty on gold and silver imports to 15% from 6% to reduce pressure on forex reserves/current account deficit and curb gold imports; hedging does not cover customs-duty hikes, so inventory gains/losses from duty changes still flow through even for hedged players like Titan. A subsequent gold/silver duty hike (2026) was flagged by analysts (Nomura, Motilal Oswal) as manageable for Titan.

rural.evidence: No direct rural revenue split disclosed in available sources. Company commentary emphasizes premiumization: Prestige & Above (P&A) segment revenue share grew from 40% in FY20 to 48% in FY25, implying the remaining ~52% is regular/popular segment (typically more rural/semi-urban weighted), but no explicit rural % was found (secondary source: equity research summary, not primary AR text).

crude_exposure.evidence: No crude oil linkage disclosed (grain/ENA/molasses-based inputs, not petroleum). Secondary-source commentary notes FY25 operating margin improvement aided by 'changes in packaging (shifting from glass to PET bottles in the regular segment)' as a cost optimization measure, and commissioning of the Sitapur distillery for backward integration into ENA (extra neutral alcohol) production — but no raw-material-cost percentage was disclosed in sources reviewed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Company describes global presence in '100+ countries' (export markets including premium Rampur whisky), implying some USD/foreign-currency revenue exposure, but no export revenue percentage or hedging policy disclosure was found in the sources accessed.

rural.evidence: Rural demand is outpacing urban demand, with the company achieving sustained double-digit underlying volume growth in both Consumer & Bazaar (C&B) and B2B segments in FY25 (from earnings-call/media commentary; exact rural revenue % not found).

crude_exposure.evidence: Pidilite imports vinyl acetate monomer (VAM), which accounts for around 60% of the company's raw material cost. FY25: Gross Margins improved by 254 bps y-o-y on account of lower input costs, aided by benign VAM prices (Q2FY25 avg VAM price ~$980/tonne vs ~$1,000/tonne in Q2FY24). EBITDA margin ~23.6% vs 22.9% prior year. (Note: 60% figure is share of raw material cost, not of total revenue; raw material cost as % of revenue not found in available sources.)

inr_exposure.evidence: VAM/VAE inputs are imported and USD/crude-linked; media commentary notes margins have historically been impacted by raw material inflation combined with a weaker rupee. Specific hedging policy disclosure not located in accessible sources (annual report PDF fetch blocked/403).

govt_capex.evidence: Business is entirely driven by government and public-sector customers (Ministry of Defence, DRDO, HAL, BEL, ECIL, BrahMos Aerospace); no significant private-sector customer base. In FY23, MoD alone contributed ~31% and DRDO ~32% of revenue (63% combined) — comparable current-year (FY24-25) customer-level split was not disclosed in sources found (company's revised FY26 annual report reportedly removed client-concentration data).

inr_exposure.evidence: Export orders were approximately 12% of the total order book in FY25 (~₹78 crore of order book), indicating a predominantly domestic (INR) revenue base with modest and growing export/USD exposure.

pli_scheme.evidence: No direct evidence found confirming Data Patterns is a named beneficiary of a PLI scheme; PLI-related import-substitution narratives found in sources refer to the broader Indian electronics/defence/API ecosystem generally, not to this company specifically.

china_plus_one.evidence: Coverage notes Bosch group pursuing a 'China Plus One' strategy globally (continuing to invest in China R&D while expanding India), and Bosch India cited 'export demand, particularly in off-highway components and software services' increasing amid 'ongoing supply chain challenges' — but no explicit statement in available sources attributing Bosch Limited India's FY25 revenue/order growth specifically to China+1 diversification.

rural.evidence: Powertrain Solutions division sales rose 5.8% in FY25 'driven by growth in the tractor segment' — tractor demand is a common proxy for rural/agri-linked demand, but no explicit rural revenue percentage was disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Auto components manufacturing implies exposure to steel, plastics and rubber (crude-derivative) input costs, but no quantified raw-material cost percentage was found in available sources.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export sales are estimated to be a small minority of Bosch Limited's revenue (third-party trade-data estimate ~7%, not an officially disclosed AR segment split — years mismatched between the export-value and revenue-value sources, so no reliable percentage recorded here). Bosch India reported FY25 net revenue of ₹18,087 crore with domestic Mobility-business sales up 6.2% and Powertrain Solutions exports also increasing, but no hedging policy detail was found.

pli_scheme.evidence: India has an Auto/Auto-components PLI scheme, but no confirmation was found in available sources that Bosch Limited (India) is a named participant or beneficiary.

china_plus_one.evidence: CEO Ajay Bhardwaj stated ahead of the IPO: 'We're now the second source for many products made in China, and the first choice for new ones,' explicitly positioning Anthem as a 'China alternative' for global biotech/pharma clients diversifying supply chains. Coverage also notes the company 'discontinued intermediates outsourcing from China and focused on backward integration for the past few years, which benefitted the gross margin.' Company achieved 24.8% revenue CAGR over five years to ₹1,844 crore in FY25 (36.8% EBITDA margin), serving 550+ clients in 44+ countries with Europe and North America as key markets — growth explicitly linked to global supply-chain diversification away from China.

inr_exposure.evidence: Company serves 550+ clients across 44+ countries (Europe and North America described as key markets), implying substantial foreign-currency-denominated revenue, but no specific USD-revenue percentage or hedging policy was disclosed in sources found.

pli_scheme.evidence: India operates a PLI scheme for bulk drugs/APIs aimed at reducing import dependence (e.g., on China), and Anthem manufactures fermentation-based APIs domestically, which is thematically relevant, but no direct confirmation was found that Anthem Biosciences is a named PLI scheme beneficiary.

rural.evidence: IHCL is expanding aggressively into Tier 2/Tier 3 cities via the Gateway (55 hotels) and Ginger (262 hotels, ₹675 crore FY25 revenue, largest growth engine) brands, citing 'rising domestic travel, infrastructure growth, and evolving consumer preferences' and demand in 'wellness/spiritual tourism.' FY25: 74 new hotels signed, 26 new openings, taking portfolio to 380 hotels; industry data cited suggests ~64% of 2025 branded hotel keys nationally are in Tier 2/3 markets. No specific tier-2/3 or rural revenue percentage was disclosed for IHCL itself.

govt_capex.evidence: Commentary attributes part of Tier 2/3 city growth to broader 'infrastructure growth' (implicitly government-led tourism/transport infrastructure), but no revenue percentage tied to government capex was disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: geography.export_pct here is repurposed as overseas-hotels revenue share (not goods exports): FY25 consolidated revenue ₹8,565 crore; overseas hotels generated ~₹1,512 crore (~17.7%), implying ~82.3% domestic. Hotel Services overall was ~91% (₹7,623 crore) of consolidated revenue. No explicit currency-hedging policy was found in sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: Search sources indicate Indian pharma generally has 70-90% dependency on Chinese key starting materials (KSMs), i.e. India functions as a downstream processor rather than a China+1 beneficiary; no JB Pharma-specific China+1 sourcing-shift narrative was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: International formulations business (Russia/CIS branded generics) exposed to RUB currency volatility; commentary noted a period of roughly -5% constant-currency growth in Russia due to currency volatility and a muted flu season. Domestic + CDMO segments together were reported as ~69-70% of FY25 revenue (9M/FY25 commentary), implying international/export formulations of roughly 30-31%, but a clean domestic-vs-export geographic split was not found in available sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: No evidence found that JB Pharma participates in the bulk-drug/API or pharma PLI schemes; company is primarily a branded-formulations and CDMO player rather than a bulk API/KSM manufacturer targeted by the PLI scheme.

china_plus_one.evidence: Analyst/industry commentary states growth opportunities have arisen 'because of the world's China plus one policy wherein many international companies prefer sourcing from India compared to China.' Company's European business (Endurance Overseas, Italy) grew 15.4% YoY in FY25 with EBITDA growth of 20.9%, outperforming the industry, consistent with export/diversification momentum, though no explicit China+1 framing was found directly attributed to Endurance in the annual report itself.

crude_exposure.evidence: Commentary notes performance was helped by 'lower raw material costs' and 'decline in high energy prices in Europe' strengthening operating margin; primary inputs are aluminium and rubber/plastics (partly petro-derived), but no explicit crude-oil-linked raw material percentage was disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Overseas revenue (~24% of consolidated FY25 revenue) is predominantly EUR-denominated via Endurance Overseas Srl (Italy) rather than USD; no hedging policy details found.

pli_scheme.evidence: Found reference to Endurance receiving an addendum to its Eligibility Certificate under Maharashtra's state 'Package Scheme of Incentives 2019' (incentives raised to Rs 858.29 crore for Waluj/Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar investments) — this is a state industrial subsidy, not confirmed participation in the central Auto/Auto-Component PLI scheme. Sample lists of PLI-Auto beneficiaries found in search (Maruti, Hero MotoCorp, Tata Autocomp, Motherson, Bosch, Lucas-TVS) did not include Endurance.

china_plus_one.evidence: Analyst commentary: 'rising preference for Indian fluorochemical suppliers amid China+1 sentiment benefits NFIL's export-led business.' Company supplies directly to the top five global innovative agrochemical companies and has signed a long-term multi-year contract (MYC) with a global agrochemical major; High-Performance Products (HPP) segment grew 26% YoY and now comprises 51% of FY25 revenue, with Specialty/CRAMS segments together contributing over 60% of revenue, attributed partly to global supply-chain diversification away from China.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key raw material is fluorspar (a mineral, not crude oil), for which Navin Fluorine is exposed to Chinese supply dominance and has sought to de-risk via long-term contracts with South African miners; refrigerant-gas (HFC) products have some petrochemical linkage but no explicit crude-oil raw-material percentage was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Business is described as 'export-led' with US alone accounting for ~20% of sales, implying material USD revenue exposure; no specific hedging policy disclosure was found in available sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: No specific evidence found that Navin Fluorine is a named beneficiary of a PLI scheme; commentary discusses general specialty-chemicals PLI policy support but does not confirm company-level participation.

rural.evidence: General industry commentary attributes Indian cement demand growth (projected 6-7% in FY25) to infrastructure, housing and industrial capex, with rural/affordable housing schemes among demand drivers industry-wide; no company-specific rural revenue percentage was disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: Industry-wide commentary: 'government's infrastructure push is a significant catalyst, with projects like the Mumbai-Ahmedabad Bullet Train Corridor significantly boosting cement demand,' and cement makers plan to invest ~Rs 1.25 lakh crore (FY25-27) to add 130 million tonnes of capacity amid sustained infra/housing demand. Company (HeidelbergCement India / Cemindia, plants in Central India - Damoh/Narsingarh/Ammasandra region) operates in this domestic infra/housing-driven demand environment, but no company-specific govt-capex revenue percentage was found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Cement manufacturing cost is sensitive to fuel/power costs (coal, pet coke, diesel for logistics) which move with crude oil prices; company reported efforts to reduce fossil dependency with Narsingarh and Ammasandra plants running on 40% and 90% renewable energy respectively, implying meaningful fossil-fuel cost exposure historically, but no explicit raw-material percentage tied to crude/fuel costs was disclosed in available sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: Cement sector is not covered by a PLI scheme; no beneficiary status applicable.
